digest_markdown:
Here are 5 bullet points about notable open-source software supply chain attacks or compromises:

* A supply chain attack targeting GitHub repositories, known as GhostAction, has been confirmed, exposing 3,325 secrets, including tokens and keys across widely used platforms. [3]
* A malicious campaign linked to the Mini Shai-Hulud activity compromised the @7nohe/openapi-react-query-codegen PyPI package, which receives roughly 150,000 weekly downloads, and stole developer credentials. [8][9]
* Two alleged TeamPCP members were arrested and charged for their alleged roles in inserting malicious code into widely used open-source software, compromising more than 1,000 organizations worldwide. [4]
* A new Shai-Hulud software supply-chain campaign compromised multiple scientific and bioinformatics packages hosted on PyPI, exposing a risk that extends far beyond individual developer workstations. [12]
* A typosquatted package on PyPI was created to abuse Python's startup mechanisms, allowing the malware to execute automatically in environments where affected packages are installed, including development systems, notebook environments, and CI/CD pipelines. [11]
